target_customer: Urban diners and office workers ordering from premium restaurants, and restaurants that wanted delivery without their own couriers
problem: Good restaurants rarely delivered. Caviar curated restaurants, photographed dishes and ran the couriers so restaurants needed no delivery infrastructure.
business_model: Marketplace take rate on restaurant orders plus a delivery fee ($9.99 flat noted at launch)

technical_complexity.rationale: A web and mobile ordering app plus courier dispatch; the hard part was operations and restaurant curation rather than engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Curation, exclusive restaurants and professional photography gave some differentiation, but Postmates, DoorDash and others quickly copied the model.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Square bought Caviar in August 2014 for $90 million in stock per Haas, and DoorDash bought it from Square in August 2019 for $410 million.

market_need_then: Seamless and Grubhub covered mainstream delivery but not high-end restaurants; Caviar reported 80% repeat orders and an average order of about $80 in 2014 across four cities.

branding.domain_note: Used trycaviar.com as its main domain (directory listing); the exact .com was not claimed by the delivery company.

identity.visual_style: Professional photography of every dish (per Haas)
identity.voice_and_tone: Premium and curated, positioned as fancy food

branding.brand_signature: Curated premium restaurants with professional dish photography
branding.community_and_virality: Press framed it as fancy food delivery; no merch or community evidence found.

brand_strength.rationale: The premium name matched the curated positioning and press covered the brand, but search for brand identity returned nothing about it and the name collides with the food product.

outcome_analysis: Caviar launched in San Francisco in July 2012 with curated restaurants, raised a $2M seed and a $13M Series A led by Tiger Global in April 2014, and sold to Square four months later for $90M in stock. Square reportedly struggled to make it profitable and sold it to DoorDash for $410M in 2019. Success reflected a strong premium niche with 80% repeat orders against crowded general delivery.
notes: Company website returned 403.
